# US Rent Tools

> US Rent Tools is a free, client-side website of US landlord and renter calculators and guides. No sign-up, no login, no paid packages or upgrades. General information only, not legal advice. City ordinances may be stricter and may override state rules.

## About

- Site: https://www.usrenttools.com/
- Purpose: Help renters and small landlords answer, in one place, how much rent is owed for a partial month, how much rent can be increased, how much security deposit can be charged, and when a deposit must be returned, under the state rules the site verifies.
- Model: Static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Calculators run in the browser. No account is required and no user data is sent to a server by the tools.
- Last verified: 2026-10-25
- Verified-rules scope: Only the rules listed below are asserted on this site. For every other state, city, or topic, the site's answer is "Check official source" for your city and state.
- Methodology: https://www.usrenttools.com/pages/methodology.html
- Editorial policy: https://www.usrenttools.com/pages/editorial-policy.html
- About: https://www.usrenttools.com/pages/about.html

## Verified rules (summary)

- Prorated rent: actual-days = rent / days in the month x days occupied; 30-day = rent / 30 x days occupied; 365-day = rent x 12 / 365 x days occupied. The method in the lease is the one that matters for a tenancy. No single federal rule prescribes a prorating method.
- California rent cap: AB 1482, Civil Code section 1947.12 - maximum increase min(5% + local CPI, 10%) per 12 months, for covered properties only.
- Washington rent cap: HB 1217, RCW 59.18.700 - no rent increase during the first 12 months after tenancy begins; after that, maximum increase min(7% + CPI, 10%), with exemptions in RCW 59.18.710.
- California security deposit: AB 12, Civil Code section 1950.5 - generally 1 month's rent, with a small-landlord exception up to 2 months as defined in the statute; return generally within 21 calendar days after vacating, with an itemized statement for deductions. AB 2801 photo documentation rule applies as stated on the site.
- Texas security deposit: Property Code sections 92.103 and 92.107 - no statutory cap on the amount (the lease controls); return within 30 days, with the duty triggered by a written forwarding address.
- Oregon late fee: ORS 90.260 - 4-day grace period; the fee must be in a written rental agreement; 5% per succeeding 5-day period as one statutory structure, not a single flat 5% overall cap.
- 3x rent rule: Required gross monthly income = rent x 3. This is a landlord/listing screening practice, not a universal federal law. The NYC 40x annual test (required annual income = rent x 40) is a separate listing rule, not a statute.
- 30% affordability rule: Maximum rent = gross income x 30%. This is a budgeting guideline, not a law.

## Worked examples used across the site

- Prorated rent: $1,800 rent, move-in October 16 (16 days occupied in a 31-day month) = $929.03 on the actual-days basis, $960.00 on the 30-day basis, $946.85 on the 365-day basis.
- 3x rent rule: $1,500 rent requires $5,000 per month gross income at 3x.
- California rent cap example: $2,000 rent at 3% CPI is capped at $2,160 (8%).
- Washington rent cap example: 7% + CPI capped at 10%; for example, 7% + 4% CPI = 11%, capped at 10%.
- California deposit example: 1 month's rent as the general limit under AB 12.

## Limitations

- General information only, not legal advice.
- City ordinances may be stricter and may override state rules. Check the official source for your city and state before acting.
- Coverage, exemptions, notice rules, and definitions are state- and city-specific. The site does not assert rules for states outside California, Washington, Oregon, and Texas.
- Calculator results depend on the figures entered. The method in the lease controls where a lease method and a calculator method differ.
